correctness.rationale: The order-preserving update forces periodic orbit states to be an antichain. Conversely the explicit positive-DNF extension realizes exactly every cyclic word whose length-n windows form an antichain. Sperner bounds the period by binom(n,floor(n/2)). For n<=6 the resulting finite periods beyond n have been exhaustively enumerated by direct 2^L enumeration and an independently implemented pruned search, both yielding 28 rooted length-7, 18 rooted length-9, and zero other above-memory cycles. The positive DNF witness realizes a length-nine orbit, and pure cycling realizes length n at all smaller widths. All boundaries n=1..6 were checked; computation is finite and fully justified by the cutoff.

value.rationale: The first register width in which cooperative monotone feedback permits a period longer than the number of memory cells is a natural dynamical threshold. The exact value nine at memory six sharpens the generic width-20 antichain bound by over a factor of two, identifies the absence of period eight, and classifies all exceptional length-seven and length-nine cycles. The result has structural use for small monotone sequential circuit designs, independent of broader unsolved n>=7 behavior.
